newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Popularity of HK future leader Tung rises -polls.
newsitem.headline: Popularity of HK future leader Tung rises -polls.

text.p: Hong Kong's future leader Tung Chee-hwa's popularity has recovered since he announced the team that will run the territory after Britain pulls out in June, two opinion polls showed on Wednesday.
In a poll of 2,435 people conducted on Monday by the independent Ming Pao newspaper, Tung scored 5.9 points for "ability" out of a full mark of nine, compared with 5.2 in a survey on February 17.
He scored 5.7 for "trustworthiness", up from 4.9 points.

The Ming Pao poll asked people to consider Tung's naming last week of his government secretaries. He retained most of the territory's incumbent senior officials, including the popular Chief Secretary Anson Chan.

In another poll of 563 people conducted on Monday for the independent Apple Daily newspaper, the leader-in-waiting scored 65.3 points on a scale of 100 in a "people's evaluation of Tung", up from 60.5 in a similar poll on January 28.
Neither newspaper gave a margin for error.

The Apple Daily poll also showed 35.9 percent of respondents thought Hong Kong would change for the better after Britain hands back the territory to Beijing at midnight on June 30, ending more than 150 years of colonial rule.
This compared with 13.5 percent in a similar poll at the end of 1995, the paper said.
Tung, 59, a Shanghai-born shipping billionaire, was picked by a Beijing-controlled committee in December to govern the capitalist territory of 6.4 million people after the handover.
His popularity jumped at the time but then slumped after he issued public statements firmly backing China's plans to trim back laws dealing with civil liberties in the territory.
